सखम्लपपिमु for ग्लापयामाः दर््रन्ति for दर्शयन्ति
'त्वाजच् for हित्वा safe for जनय
afse for बद्धा Rafe for Arve
zfa for qraifd arafw for awa
उपेन्ति for उपयन्ति पूरेदि for wa

_:It may be remarked that the corruptions above
quoted are, in many instances, the precursors of forms
adopted in other affiliated dialects. In Sanskrit the
third person singular of the verb ४० be is Bhavatt,
which in the Gatha changes to Bhoti by the conversion
of the v into ० and the elision of the ¢ before and after
it, (Bhonti in the plural and hos? in the second person
singular, ) and thence we have hoti, hosiand hontd in the
Magadhi; Hae and Haen in the Khariboli, and dhe, ahet
and ahes in the Marhatti. In the Hindi, notwith-
standing the re-duplication of the root in hotdhae, the
original form is still distinctly indicated. S’unitvd for
s‘ruivd is the first step to the formation of s’unid in
Bengali, while s’uzoht passes into s’uno with nothing
but the elision of an inflection, which in the original
Sanskrit, is oftener omitted than retained.

In connexion with this part of my subject the
following remarks of Dr. John Muir will be read
with interest. I quote them from the second volume
of his invaluable ‘ Sanskrit Texts,’ pp. 119 to 122.

५५ There are, however, some other forms discoverable in the Gatha
dialect, which have been cither passed over, or but bricfly noticed
by Babu Raéjendralal, and which yet present some points of remark-
able interest. Thus the plural instrumental im ebhzh, which is so

general in the Vedas, is in constant use in the Gathds also, as in the
instances s’éhiyeblith, sattvebhih, qunebhih, simhdsanebhih, dérakebhih
